title: The Chemical Drain Cleaner Myth
description: Many property owners believe that pouring harsh chemical drain cleaners down a slow-running fixture is the best first step for troubleshooting drainage systems. In reality, these caustic or acid-based chemicals often fail to clear stubborn clogs like grease and wipes, and they can sit stagnantly in trapped sections of pipe, corroding metal joints and degrading older materials. Furthermore, if the chemical fails to clear the blockage, it creates a severe safety hazard for the professional plumber who must later service or snake the line, risking chemical splashes. Professional drainage troubleshooting starts with mechanical clearing methods, such as augers or hydro-jetting, which physically remove the obstruction without risking chemical burns or pipe damage.

The Chemical Drain Cleaner Myth

Many property owners believe that pouring harsh chemical drain cleaners down a slow-running fixture is the best first step for troubleshooting drainage systems. In reality, these caustic or acid-based chemicals often fail to clear stubborn clogs like grease and wipes, and they can sit stagnantly in trapped sections of pipe, corroding metal joints and degrading older materials. Furthermore, if the chemical fails to clear the blockage, it creates a severe safety hazard for the professional plumber who must later service or snake the line, risking chemical splashes. Professional drainage troubleshooting starts with mechanical clearing methods, such as augers or hydro-jetting, which physically remove the obstruction without risking chemical burns or pipe damage.
